content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (Zucchini) is a young, tender variety of squash, usually light green or yellow. When cooked it retains a soft texture and a mild sweet flavor. It is used in soups, stews, side dishes and as an ingredient in baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is a close relative of cucumber.
Unlike mature pumpkins, young fruits contain less sugar and more water.
In Italy it is called “zucchini” and often served as “zoodles” – thin strips used like pasta.
Summer squash is rich in antioxidants, especially lutein and zeaxanthin.
In Japan it appears in the traditional dish “kabu-no-tai” (stewed squash).

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cooked summer squash provides about 17 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin A as beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is important for eye health and skin.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to summer squash.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, rinse thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

items.title: Excess sodium from added salt
items.content: Adding salt during cooking can increase sodium content, which should be limited in hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Summer squash can be boiled, steamed, roasted, or sautéed. It is added to soups, stews, salads, pasta dishes, and used as a filling for pancakes or pies. Before cooking, trim the ends and cut into cubes, slices, or ribbons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked summer squash in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags – it keeps its flavor and texture for up to 2 months.
